name: EMSculpt muscle stimulation

card.summary: A clinic device that triggers intense muscle contractions with focused electromagnetic energy to tone muscle and, with the Neo version, add heat to reduce fat.
card.aka: EMSCULPT, EMSCULPT NEO, HIFEM, high-intensity focused electromagnetic therapy, BTL
card.note: Published studies are small and many are industry-linked; systematic reviews describe the evidence as limited.

quick.overview:
EMSCULPT, made by BTL Industries, uses high-intensity focused electromagnetic (HIFEM) energy to cause supramaximal muscle contractions in the abdomen, buttocks and other areas. The aim is to increase muscle tone or mass. EMSCULPT NEO adds radiofrequency heating to also reduce fat.

Published studies include MRI and multi-center buttock studies, and systematic reviews that assess efficacy and safety of electromagnetic treatments for body contouring.
quick.mechanism: A magnetic field induces involuntary muscle contractions stronger than voluntary ones. The manufacturer and researchers report that this can thicken muscle and, in the NEO version, add radiofrequency heat to reduce fat.
quick.risks: The reviewed literature describes few adverse effects, but evidence is limited and the early studies are small. The EMSCULPT NEO device is described as FDA-cleared for muscle toning and fat reduction in a 2024 systematic review.

lead: EMSCULPT (BTL Industries) is a non-invasive body-contouring treatment that uses high-intensity focused electromagnetic (HIFEM) energy to stimulate muscle contractions in areas such as the abdomen and buttocks. A 2024 systematic review describes EMSCULPT NEO as an FDA-cleared treatment for increasing muscle tone and reducing fat, in which HIFEM builds muscle mass and combined radiofrequency is intended to reduce fat.[1]

For people who want a more defined midsection or a lifted, firmer rear without surgery, the pitch is that the applicator held over the area drives repeated powerful muscle contractions, which the manufacturer and its investigators say thicken the muscle and thin the overlying fat. A typical course described in reviews is four sessions over about two weeks.[4]

Early studies include a 22-patient abdominal study evaluated with MRI that introduced HIFEM and established hypotheses for future research,[2] and a multi-center study of 75 patients examining toning and lifting of gluteal muscles.[3] Systematic reviews of electromagnetic treatments for body contouring have since been published, with differing conclusions about the size of the measured changes.[4][1][5]

paras: HIFEM technology induces muscle contractions that the first MRI study of the abdomen described as having a dual tissue effect, on both muscle and fat.[2] EMSCULPT NEO combines electromagnetic energy with radiofrequency, intended to build muscle mass while reducing fat.[1]

Proponents describe the contractions as far stronger than a person can produce voluntarily, which is the reason given for muscle growth and for the fat changes seen on imaging.[2][9] The manufacturer also introduced smaller applicators shaped for arms and calves; in a 2019 announcement a trial investigator described the higher energy field as aimed at small areas while limiting stimulation of neighbouring muscles.[9]

The main targets are the abdomen and buttocks, with thighs, flanks, upper arms and calves also treated in published studies.[2][3][5] In a 2019 announcement of an arms and calves clearance, BTL described demand from patients and physicians for tough-to-target areas, and investigator Bruce Katz said there had not previously been an effective non-invasive option for them.[9]

The gluteal study asked 75 patients aged 22 to 59 to rate their buttocks before and after four 30-minute treatments; the satisfaction score rose from about 13 at baseline to about 18 afterwards on a 4 to 28 scale.[3]

In the abdominal study, 22 patients received four treatments and were evaluated with anthropometry, photographs and MRI.[2] The MRI analysis reported an average 18.6 percent reduction of adipose tissue thickness, a 15.4 percent increase in rectus abdominis muscle thickness and a 10.4 percent reduction in separation of the abdominal muscles two months after treatment.[2]

A 2023 systematic review in Annals of Plastic Surgery evaluated 14 studies, mostly of the original device, and reported a mean fat thickness reduction of 5.5 mm and a mean muscle thickness increase of 2.2 mm; its authors described photographic results as typically modest and measurement variance as high.[4] A 2025 review of seven studies of EMSCULPT NEO reported a mean fat thickness reduction of 8.0 mm and a mean muscle thickness increase of 5.5 mm, noted that all seven were authored by BTL medical advisors, and concluded that the measured changes were likely within the margin of error and of questionable clinical relevance.[5] A 2024 systematic review addressed HIFEM with and without radiofrequency.[1] BTL and its investigators, by contrast, describe the findings as significant, citing the statistical tests used in the studies.[2]

BTL launched EMSCULPT in 2018 for abdomen and buttocks, and announced clearance for arms and calves in July 2019.[9] The EMSCULPT NEO, which adds radiofrequency, followed, and BTL has marketed it as FDA-cleared for muscle toning and fat reduction.[1] Systematic reviews began appearing in 2023.[4]

The 2023 review reported that no complications were recorded across the studies it evaluated, and the 2025 review noted few adverse events.[4][5] Manufacturer instructions list contraindications related to implants and electronic devices; users should consult the product's labelling.

Human studies include the MRI abdominal study,[2] the gluteal multi-center study,[3] and systematic reviews.[4][1][5] Of the 14 studies in the 2023 review, 11 used the original EMSCULPT, two used EMSCULPT NEO and one included a sham group.[4] Two registered buttock-lifting trials with a magnetic device were withdrawn.[6][7] Other registered HIFEM trials concern back pain.[8] Many device studies are small, and the reviews describe differing views on how large the effects are.

chain: Electromagnetic pulses trigger supramaximal muscle contractions
Muscle thickens and, with radiofrequency in NEO, overlying fat thins
angle.text: The treatment is used as a passive, session-based way to tone abdominal and gluteal muscle and trim the fat layer above it. Studies measured this with MRI, ultrasound and photographs, and with patient satisfaction questionnaires for the buttocks.
